ages.title: International, year and counting age
items: International age starts at 0 and adds a year on each birthday. Since June 28, 2023, Korean laws, contracts and documents use it.
Year age is the current year minus the birth year. Some laws, such as youth protection and military service, still use it.
Counting age is year age plus one and is no longer used officially.

zodiac.title: When the sign changes
items: The zodiac and sexagenary year change at Lunar New Year, so January and February births can fall in the previous sign.
Lunar New Year 2027 is February 7, so births from Jan 1 to Feb 6, 2027 are the 2026 Red Horse.
Saju may divide the year at Ipchun (around Feb 4), which can differ from the Lunar New Year rule.
The heavenly stem sets the color: gap/eul blue, byeong/jeong red, mu/gi yellow, gyeong/sin white, im/gye black.

school.title: School entry year
items: Children start elementary school in March of the year after they turn 6. Entrants in March 2027 were born in 2020.
Until the 2008 school year the cut-off was March 1, so January–February births entered a year early. Those born Jan–Feb 2002 were the last.
Early entry or deferral changes the year.

items.a: Jeongmi, the Red Goat. The sign changes at Lunar New Year (Feb 7, 2027), so births from Jan 1 to Feb 6, 2027 are Horse.
International age counts from the birthday; year age subtracts the birth year. Laws use international age since June 28, 2023, though some still use year age.

items.q: Until when were children enrolled early?
items.a: Until the 2008 school year, January–February births entered a year early. Those born Jan–Feb 2002 were the last.
Children born between Jan 1 and Dec 31, 2020, starting in March 2027.
